title: BrightCart QBR / Health Check
summary: Quarterly health check focused on usage trends, cost drivers, recent reliability incidents, roadmap alignment for Dedicated deployment, and next steps for a pilot on Private/VPC. Action items include sharing cost breakdown, SOC2 docs, and scheduling a dedicated benchmark with their infra team.
next_steps: Redwood to share last 90-day cost-by-route spreadsheet (Maya)
SE to run dedicated benchmark with BrightCart infra (Liam + Raj)
Send SOC 2 + security pack to BrightCart legal (Jordan)
Follow-up meeting to review benchmark results and pilot plan in two weeks (calendar invite from Maya)
action_items: Maya Chen: share cost breakdown spreadsheet by 2025-03-07
Liam O'Connor: coordinate benchmark run and provide test harness by 2025-03-12
Jordan Wu: send SOC2/ISO docs and encryption/KMS notes by 2025-03-06
Raj Patel: provide sample traffic profile and credentials for testing by 2025-03-08
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-03-05
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Jordan Wu (Redwood CSM), Elena Garcia (BrightCart Head of ML), Raj Patel (Platform Eng), Sofia Martinez (CTO)

Summary (auto): quick QBR, looked at usage trends, two brief reliability incidents in Feb, discussed Dedicated vs Private, agreed to run a benchmark and share cost breakdown and security pack.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we know folks are busy so we'll try to keep this tight, quick QBR slash health check for BrightCart. I'm Maya, AE, with Liam our SE and Jordan CSM.
[00:18] Sofia: hey thanks Maya, afternoon all.
[00:20] Elena: hi, good to see you.
[00:22] Raj: morning from my side.
[00:25] Maya: great. Quick agenda — usage & cost trends, any reliability incidents, roadmap alignment for your Dedicated plan, and then next steps. does that sound right?
[00:33] Elena: yes that works. we mostly want to understand recent cost increases and what options we have for lowering unit cost without hurting latency for checkout flows.
[00:45] Liam: understood. We'll start with the numbers Jordan pulled together. Jordan?
[00:50] Jordan: yep, so over the last 90 days we see token consumption up ~38% month-over-month for the recommender routes, and cost is up about 42% primarily due to more regen calls after the A/B test changes you shipped. there's also a small uptick in long-context chat sessions which amplify per-request tokens.
[01:12] Elena: ok that aligns with our dashboard; the regen was intentional but we didn't expect it to double server-side cost. Is there a way to cache more aggressively?
[01:22] Liam: yes — a couple levers. you can enable prefix/KV caching for deterministic segments of the prompt and also tune batching windows. we recommended a cache TTL on the recommender prefix, and a small batch delay (20-40ms) that still meets your 95th pct latency for checkout.
[01:38] Raj: we're worried about added latency with batching. our SLO is <=200ms p95 for checkout calls.
[01:45] Liam: totally fair. in our tests, small batching (20ms) increased p95 by ~12-18ms but reduced cost per token materially. Also consider mixing in a quantized model variant for non-critical long-context flows — lower precision model for background recommendations, keep full-precision for checkout-specific paths.
[02:06] Elena: can you remind me which models you've seen work with our setup? our current routes use an LLaMA-derivative that was tuned in-house.
[02:16] Maya: sure. From the model catalog, your checkout flow is using rwd-llama-v1-16b (approx naming), and for background you could move to rwd-qlora-8b-ptq which is much cheaper. Liam has some perf profiles.
[02:30] Liam: right, the 8b-ptq gives 2-3x token cost reduction in Dedicated if you can accept slightly lower fluency for background recs. We'll include the perf sheet.
[02:42] Sofia: on Dedicated — we're under a reserved capacity contract for the next 6 months. is there anything we should change in autoscaling to avoid throttles?
[02:52] Jordan: you currently have a burst buffer enabled but set fairly low. Given the recent traffic spikes during flash sales, increasing burst capacity by one GPU equivalent reduced throttles in a customer we onboarded last month.
[03:08] Raj: question on private deployment: we heard from infra that they prefer a VPC private control plane for compliance reasons. what's involved to move to Private?
[03:18] Liam: Private (VPC) is definitely doable — requires network peering or private link, KMS integration for keys, and a short on-prem or VPC agent install. There are some audit log export configs and an on-boarding checklist. We can run a pilot with your infra team; typical time is 4-6 weeks depending on approvals.
[03:37] Elena: what about SOC2 / ISO docs? legal asked for them last week.
[03:41] Jordan: we'll send the SOC2 report, ISO attestation, and our security pack. I'll include notes on RBAC, SAML SSO, and key management.
[03:50] Sofia: great. Last week we saw two brief timeouts — one on Feb 11 and one on Feb 24 — were those on your side?
[03:58] Maya: we traced Feb 11 to a misrouted traffic flap in a midwest region; the Feb 24 one was an infra OOM on an early model variant during a stress test. both were below your SLA but still noisy.
[04:12] Liam: for the OOM we adjusted kernel settings and rolling restart sequence, and added guardrails to the model launcher to avoid noisy neighbor memory spikes. we can share the postmortem.
[04:23] Raj: that would help. Also, we've been seeing more 5xx errors around large context prompts — could be KV cache evictions?
[04:33] Liam: possibly. sometimes the tokenizer differences or odd unicode chars cause desyncs; also KV cache eviction thresholds if you hit concurrency. we'll ask for the stack traces and attach them to the benchmark run.
[04:48] Elena: ok. On the benchmark — what do you need from us?
[04:52] Liam: sample traffic profile (payload sizes, p95 latency targets, concurrency), a small test account with representative secrets, and a time window to run the load. Raj can coordinate.
[05:03] Raj: I can provide sample traffic and a staging VPC endpoint. security will want ephemeral creds.
[05:09] Jordan: we'll accept ephemeral creds and have a checklist for security.
[05:12] Maya: perfect. a couple more things — pricing. we can model the cost reductions with batching + quantization and show expected monthly savings. we'll share a spreadsheet.
[05:22] Elena: that would be super helpful.
[05:25] Sofia: one more ask: we plan a roadmap item to support always-on checkout inference at peak times — we need to understand tail latency guarantees under load. can Redwood provide a tail latency report?
[05:37] Liam: yes we can produce a p95/p99 breakdown under your traffic shape; we'll run that in the dedicated benchmark. note p99 can be sensitive to network jitter — if you want stronger guarantees, we can discuss a hot-standby approach or pin GPUs for the checkout model.
[05:53] Raj: what's the uplift cost for GPU pinning? ballpark.
[05:57] Maya: depends on instance type; roughly 20-35% premium for reserved pinned capacity vs. shared Dedicated. we'll include examples in the cost breakdown.
[06:10] Elena: sounds fair.
[06:13] Maya: ok let's do quick recap and action items. Jordan, you're sending SOC2 and security pack by Thursday?
[06:19] Jordan: yes, sending by 2025-03-06.
[06:22] Maya: Liam will run the benchmark and produce a perf/tail-latency report target date 2025-03-12?
[06:28] Liam: yes, target 3/12 but I'll sync with Raj for scheduling.
[06:33] Maya: I'll share the 90-day cost spreadsheet and pricing scenarios by 3/7. Raj will provide sample traffic and ephemeral creds by 3/8.
[06:40] Raj: yep.
[06:42] Elena: any blockers from Redwood side for the pilot?
[06:45] Liam: none, just the creds and the profile. we'll try to keep the load to staging.
[06:50] Sofia: ok, appreciate the clarity.
[06:53] Maya: thanks everyone. We'll send notes and calendar for the benchmark follow-up.
[06:58] Elena: thanks, bye.
[07:00] Meeting ends.

Notes: transcription has some recognition quirks ("K V cash" for KV cache, "rwd-qlora" sometimes transcribed as "reload-qlora"). References: shared cost sheet (link: shorturl.at/brightcart-costs), perf sheet (link: shorturl.at/brightcart-perf), SOC2 pack (attachment to be sent).

Recap (auto): 1) Cost increase driven by regen calls and long-context usage. 2) Improvements: prefix/KV caching, batching, quantized model for background. 3) Reliability: two incidents investigated; postmortem and mitigations to be shared. 4) Next steps: send cost breakdown, security docs, and run dedicated benchmark with BrightCart infra in two weeks.
